newsitem.title: HONG KONG: H.K. gov't 96/97 land revenue seen over HK$36 bln.
newsitem.headline: H.K. gov't 96/97 land revenue seen over HK$36 bln.

text.p: Government revenue from land transactions in Hong Kong for the current fiscal year (April-March) was likely to exceed the forecast of HK$36 billion, Director of Lands Bob Pope said on Friday.
Addressing a seminar on property investment in Hong Kong, Pope said the previous estimate had been too conservative given the activity surrounding the construction of the new Chek Lap Kok airport.

"Due to the large developments above the airport railway stations serving the new airport there has been a larger amount of land disposed of by private treaty grant to the Mass Transit Railway Corporation who in turn tender out development contracts with consortia of local and overseas developers," Pope said.
Of the $36 billion forecast, only $13 billion would come from sales by public auction or tender, Pope said.

He said total revenue from land transactions had been HK$157 billion over the past five years. The figure included $80 billion from sales by auction, $31 billion from sales by private treaty and $46 billion from lease modifications and exchanges.
Pope said long-term prospects were good.

"Property supply figures are expected to increase from 1997 onwards," he said. "Major infrastructure projects spanning 1992 to 2001 are underway or planned with the HK$158.2 billion airport and related road and rail systems entering their final stages."
Recent government land auctions have seen keen bidding from large property developers and the property sector has underpinned a record-setting rise in the stock market.
A 4,206-square-metre non-industrial site in Yuen Long in the New Territories was auctioned on Wednesday for HK$370 million, against the expected range of HK$260 million to HK$320 million.
